claim: Board 784:4480 'Publish · not-connected' says 'Connect Vercel to publish.' with a 'Connect Vercel' CTA, and its caption 788:4321 explains it as 'No Vercel connection. Publishing is impossible without it.'
truth: This panel state is NOT the missing-Vercel state. The panel renders it when the PUBLISH FEATURE FLAG is off, i.e. when no publish handler was passed at all. A missing Vercel connection renders the wizard instead (board 893:4518). With the flag off, pressing 'Connect Vercel' opens the dashboard integrations page and changes nothing — connecting Vercel does not turn publishing on. And because only the NEXT_PUBLIC_ half of the flag reaches a production bundle, this is the panel every real user sees whenever NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_PUBLISH is unset.
evidence: PublishTab.tsx:160 `const canPublish = !!onVercelPublish`; PublishTab.tsx:312-318 `const noPublishPath = !canPublish` with the comment 'board 784:4480 ... is the panel with no publish path at all — onVercelPublish absent, i.e. publishing not wired' and 'It is NOT the panel for connected-account-missing. That case has its own board, 893:4518'; TabRouter.tsx:195 `onVercelPublish={isFeatureEnabled("publish") ? onVercelPublish : undefined}`; featureFlags.ts:14 `publish: FEATURE_PUBLISH`; runtimeEnv.ts:85-86 `FEATURE_PUBLISH = (vite.VITE_FEATURE_PUBLISH ?? proc.NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_PUBLISH) === 'true'`. The real Vercel check is publish.service.ts:59-65 (label 'Vercel connected', status 'fail', detail 'Sites deploy to your own Vercel account. Connect it to publish.'), rendered by PublishWizard.tsx:182-198 and banded at :200-216 as board 893:4518 draws it. Searched by constant, not call site: VERCEL_CHECK_LABEL (packages/shared/schemas/publish.ts:76) has exactly two readers, PublishTab.tsx:330 and PublishConfirmFacts.tsx:149.
edit: Rename 784:4480 to 'Publish · unavailable (feature off)'. Change the heading text from 'Connect Vercel to publish.' to 'Publishing is turned off for this editor.' and the body from 'Buildrick deploys into your own Vercel account — we host nothing.' to 'This build has no publish path wired. Ask an admin to enable publishing.' Change the footer CTA label from 'Connect Vercel' to a non-action or a 'Learn more' link — a Connect CTA here cannot unblock anything. Rewrite caption 788:4321 from 'No Vercel connection. Publishing is impossible without it, so the panel asks for the connection instead of showing a button that would fail.' to 'Publishing is not wired in this build (NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_PUBLISH off). The missing-Vercel-connection case is board 893:4518, not this one.'

truth: Exactly right, including the order, the labels, the severities and the two affordance kinds. runPrePublishChecks pushes those six in that order; only 'Vercel connected' and 'Pages ready' can be `fail`, the other four are `warning` only; `ready = !hasFail`. NOT ONE of the six is about CMS or dynamic pages — MOD-A-11 confirmed and re-confirmed here — and neither board draws one, so there is nothing to mark unimplemented.

Order: VERCEL_CHECK_LABEL (:57-65, fail branch at :61), 'Pages ready' (:67-72, fail at :69), 'SEO configured' (:74-78, warning), 'Domain connected' (:80-85, warning), 'Empty pages' (:87-91, warning), 'Favicon' (:93-105, warning). `const hasFail = checks.some(c => c.status === 'fail'); return { ready: !hasFail, checks }` (:107-108). truth: The wizard has three more states the board does not draw, and one of them is a hole in the gate: while the checks are loading, `rows` is empty, so `blocked` is false and 'Continue to Confirm →' is ENABLED — the user can walk past the gate before it has answered. The other two are a Retry state when the fetch throws, and a 'no site' state when the editor was not opened from a site URL.

No-site branch :176-180 ('Open this site from the dashboard to see readiness checks.'). Panel-side states at PublishTab.tsx:274-284 (`checkState` 'loading' | 'ready' | 'error') and the DF5 rule at PublishService.ts:225-229 ('THROWS on a fetch error so the panel shows couldn't load · Retry rather than a fake-passing checklist').

claim: Board 784:4403 'Publish · failed' prints 'Build error on Menu — 3 unresolved links. Nothing was deployed.', and caption 788:4320 says the state 'Names the failing page and the reason, and keeps the button live so the fix-and-retry loop is one click.'
truth: The panel prints the job's raw `error` string and appends 'Nothing was deployed.' itself. That string is never page-scoped and is usually an internal code: VERCEL_NOT_CONNECTED, VERCEL_TOKEN_INVALID, VERCEL_DEPLOY_<state>, WORKER_DISPATCH_FAILED, STRANDED_BY_WORKER_DISPATCH_LOSS, SITE_NOT_FOUND, 'No page content to deploy. Open the site in the editor and publish from there.', or a raw Zod message such as 'Page HTML exceeds 2097152 bytes'. Nothing anywhere validates links, so 'Build error on Menu — 3 unresolved links' is a sentence the product cannot produce. And retry is not one click: 'Try again' resets the job and re-opens the WIZARD at its Review step, so the loop is Try again → Continue to Confirm → Publish now.
evidence: PublishTab.tsx:337-341 renders `{error}` then appends ' Nothing was deployed.' when the message does not already contain it. Error producers: publish.service.ts:314 VERCEL_NOT_CONNECTED, :678 VERCEL_TOKEN_INVALID, :671 `VERCEL_DEPLOY_${ready.readyState}`, :396 WORKER_DISPATCH_FAILED, :233 STRANDED_BY_WORKER_DISPATCH_LOSS, :268 SITE_NOT_FOUND; worker route.ts:101-103 'No page content to deploy…'; worker route.ts:201 writes `error: message` verbatim. Size messages: packages/shared/schemas/publish.ts:30 and :55. Retry: PublishTab.tsx:344-352 `onClick={() => { publishJob?.reset?.(); setWizardOpen(true); }}` — the wizard always reopens on step 'review' (PublishWizard.tsx:119-121).
edit: On 784:4403 replace the sample error line 'Build error on Menu — 3 unresolved links. Nothing was deployed.' with a string of the shape the product actually emits, e.g. 'VERCEL_TOKEN_INVALID. Nothing was deployed.' Rewrite caption 788:4320 to: 'Nothing was deployed. The line is the job's own error string — an internal code, never a page name; no link validation exists. Try again re-opens the pre-publish wizard, so retry is three clicks, not one.'

claim: Caption 788:4316 for board 778:4238 'Publish · loading' says 'The publish button is disabled until we know what is actually live — never publish into uncertainty.'
truth: The CTA is not disabled while the panel is loading. It is disabled only while a publish is in flight, immediately after one lands, or when the deploy-history read failed. During `snapshot.loading` and during `checkState === 'loading'` the button is live, and pressing it opens the wizard whose Continue is also live (see FIG-C-03). The board's own intent is right; the code does not implement it.
evidence: PublishTab.tsx:687 `disabled={isPublishing || justPublished || snapshot.error}` — `snapshot.loading` is not in that expression. The loading skeletons that DO render are PublishTab.tsx:524, :551, :594 (`snapshot.loading ? <SkeletonRows …>`), so the panel knows it is loading and simply does not gate on it. Board 778:4238 read live: it draws the three section headers with no values and the CTA 'Publish to production'.
edit: Two options; pick one and record it. (a) Keep the design and rewrite caption 788:4316 to state the gap: 'Deploy state unknown. The button SHOULD be disabled here; the shipping panel leaves it live (PublishTab.tsx:687 gates on isPublishing / justPublished / snapshot.error only).' (b) Change the board to draw the CTA in its live state and drop the sentence. Recommend (a) — the caption is the intent record and the intent is correct.

claim: Board 784:4250 prints 'Building · step 2 of 4 · started 14s ago' and caption 788:4318 says 'Progress is step-based, not a spinner, so the user knows how far along a multi-minute deploy is.'
truth: The step line can never render. The panel looks for a step whose status is 'running'; the worker writes 'active' for the step in flight. So `runningStep` is always null and the line degrades to the raw percentage. Separately the pipeline has FIVE steps, not four, and two of them ('Optimizing images', 'Performance check') are never run and report 'skipped'.
evidence: PublishTab.tsx:238-243 `const i = steps.findIndex(s => s.status === 'running')` vs worker route.ts:42-51 `buildSteps` — `if (i === activeIndex) return { name, status: failed ? 'failed' : 'active' }`. Fallback at PublishTab.tsx:493-498. Five steps at route.ts:21-27 (Generating pages, Optimizing images, Deploying to CDN, Verifying SSL, Performance check); SKIPPED_STEPS = {1, 4} at route.ts:34-37. Already filed as W-D-15 for the prototype layer; this row adds the step COUNT and the skipped pair.
edit: On 784:4250 change 'Building · step 2 of 4 · started 14s ago' to 'Deploying to CDN · step 3 of 5 · started 14s ago'. Rewrite caption 788:4318 to: 'In flight. Five steps; two of them (Optimizing images, Performance check) never run and report skipped. The step line does not render in the shipping build — the panel reads status "running" and the worker writes "active" (W-D-15), so it falls back to a percentage.'

claim: Caption 788:4319 for board 784:4326 'Publish · live' says the state 'Confirms the version, offers the live site and a diff against the previous version.'
truth: 'Compare v14 → v15' does not open a diff of those two versions. It emits a tab switch to History and nothing carries the two job ids across, so the user lands on the History tab's Published view and has to find the pair again. A real page-by-page diff exists server-side and is reachable, but this control does not call it.

The real diff is publish.service.ts getPublishDiff (:519-556) exposed as sites.publishDiff (server/trpc/routers/sites.ts:466-476) and wrapped by PublishService.fetchPublishDiff (:254-256) — none of which this button touches. "Compare v14 → v15" only switches to the History tab — it carries no job ids and opens no diff (PublishTab.tsx:475-484), although sites.publishDiff exists.' claim: All four panel boards (641:2652, 784:4250, 784:4326, 784:4403) draw an ENVIRONMENT section with two rows — 'Production · bellacucina.com ›' and 'Preview · brk-preview.vercel.app ›' — both with a chevron implying a link.
truth: There is no preview environment anywhere in the product. The snapshot hard-codes the Preview row's value to null, so the row always renders the literal 'None' with no chevron and no link. Every deployment this product creates is a production deployment; nothing ever creates or reads a Vercel preview deployment. The row is drawn as a working link to a URL that cannot exist.

Renderer PublishTab.tsx:530-531 `<EnvRow label={snapshot.preview.label} value={snapshot.preview.value} empty='None' />`; EnvRow (:89-110) draws the chevron only in the `value && href` branch, and no href is passed for Preview. Deploy target is fixed: lib/vercel.ts:140 `target: "production"`. Grepped for a preview-deployment producer by name — no `target: "preview"`, no preview URL read, anywhere in lib/vercel.ts or publish.service.ts.

claim: Board 641:2652's SINCE LAST DEPLOY rows carry per-change attribution — 'Menu — price updates · Sara · 2m', 'Hero — new photo · Sara · 41m', 'Contact — form fields · Imran · 3h'.
truth: No attribution can ever render. The change rows come from the local undo stack, whose display entries carry `userId` and never `author`; the snapshot reads `.author`, which is always undefined, so every row prints the relative time alone. The label is also an undo-action label ('Move element', 'Checkpoint'), not a page-scoped summary — the shape the board draws implies a change feed the product does not have.
evidence: usePublishSnapshot.ts:156-166 maps the stack with `author: (e as { author?: string }).author`; the entry type is HistoryDisplayEntry (historyTypes.ts:84-99) whose only attribution field is `userId: string | null`, and HistoryFormatter.ts:28-36 sets `userId: entry.userId ?? null` and never writes `author`. Render at PublishTab.tsx:610-613 `{c.author ? `${c.author} · ${c.when}` : c.when}`. Labels come from `formatTransactionLabel` / `generateLabelFromEntry` (HistoryFormatter.ts:22-25, :44-49). usePublishSnapshot's own header comment (:9-12) admits the gap.
edit: On 641:2652 remove the author names from the three change rows, leaving 'Menu — price updates · 2m' etc. If attribution is to stay as an aspiration, keep it on ONE row only and add a caption note: 'Author is not produced — the undo stack carries userId and the panel reads author (usePublishSnapshot.ts:164), so the column is always empty.' Recommend removing it: a column that is empty in 100% of renders reads as broken data, not as an aspiration.

claim: Board 641:2652 draws SINCE LAST DEPLOY as '14 changes · 3 pages' over a list of edits, and the design has no state for the section not knowing.
truth: The change count is read from the in-memory undo stack, which is empty on every fresh load. So a user who edits, saves, closes the editor and reopens it sees '0 changes' and the panel prints 'Nothing has changed since the last deploy.' over a site that has real unpublished work. The durable answer exists and the panel does not use it: fetchSitePublishState compares Site.lastEditedAt against lastPublishedAt and returns hasUnpublishedChanges, which the TOPBAR consumes and this panel does not.
evidence: usePublishSnapshot.ts:157 `const stack = composer?.history?.getHistoryStack?.() ?? []` → HistoryManager.ts:658-660 → buildHistoryDisplayEntries(this.undoStack); `undoStack` is declared `private undoStack: HistoryEntry[] = []` at HistoryManager.ts:34 and is never hydrated from any persisted source (its only assignments are the push sites :209,:218,:309,:355,:363,:590 and the reset at :156). The durable signal: PublishService.ts:160-175 fetchSitePublishState → `hasUnpublishedChanges: editedAt.getTime() > publishedAt.getTime()`, consumed at StudioHeader.tsx:590-596 and never by usePublishSnapshot. The zero-change copy is PublishTab.tsx:618-632.
edit: Clone 641:2652 into section 1776:8378 as 'Publish · panel · changes-unknown' (280x812). Same three sections; SINCE LAST DEPLOY shows no count pair and no rows, and one muted line: 'Edited since the last deploy — this session has no change list.' Keep LAST DEPLOY unchanged. Add a caption: 'A reopened editor has an empty undo stack, so the count is 0 and the panel currently claims nothing has changed. The server already answers this (hasUnpublishedChanges, PublishService.ts:172).'

claim: Board 784:4403 is the only failure state in the section, and it is worded as a deploy that ran and broke.
truth: A second publish attempted while one is already running is refused BEFORE a job exists, and the editor routes that refusal into exactly this board: the panel reads 'Publish failed. A publish job is already in progress. Nothing was deployed.' Nothing failed — another deploy is mid-flight — and 'Try again' will hit the same refusal until that one settles. There is no board for it.
evidence: publish.service.ts:206-208 `if (existing) throw new Error('ALREADY_PUBLISHING')` (and the P2002 translation at :348-351); server/trpc/routers/sites.ts:339-343 maps it to TRPCError CONFLICT 'A publish job is already in progress.'; usePublishJob.ts:204-212 catches it, `classifyPublishBlock` returns null for it (BLOCK_BY_MESSAGE at :70-75 only matches the four PUBLISH_APPROVAL_MESSAGES), so it lands in `error`; usePublishJob.ts:299-310 `: error ? 'failed'` with no jobId. PublishTab.tsx:330-341 then renders the failure section with that message.
edit: Clone 784:4403 into section 1776:8378 as 'Publish · already-publishing' (280x812). Heading in ink, not error red: 'A publish is already running.' Meta: 'Started elsewhere or in another tab. Nothing new was sent.' One action only — 'Watch it' (opens the in-flight progress) — and no 'Try again', which cannot succeed. Add a caption naming the source: server/trpc/routers/sites.ts:339-343 CONFLICT.

claim: No board covers a publish rejected for size, and the failed board's copy assumes a human-readable reason.
truth: The publish input is validated by three Zod limits and every one of them surfaces to the user as a raw schema sentence in the failure state: 'Page HTML exceeds 2097152 bytes', 'Total HTML payload exceeds 16777216 bytes', or an array-max refusal above 500 pages. This is reachable in normal use — the Optimize action rewrites a library image's src to a full base64 data URL that is never re-uploaded, so a handful of optimised images pushes a page over 2 MB (MOD-C-18).
evidence: packages/shared/schemas/publish.ts:12 MAX_PAGE_HTML_BYTES = 2*1024*1024, :15 MAX_PUBLISH_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 16*1024*1024, :18 MAX_PUBLISH_PAGES = 500; the refines at :25-31 (message `Page HTML exceeds ${MAX_PAGE_HTML_BYTES} bytes`) and :46-56 (`Total HTML payload exceeds …`), and `.max(MAX_PUBLISH_PAGES)` at :40. The message reaches the panel by the same path as FIG-C-11: usePublishJob.ts:204-212 → `error` → PublishTab.tsx:337. The data-URL inflation is MOD-C-18 (MediaLibraryPanel.tsx:318-324, MediaManager.ts:1160-1216).
edit: Clone 784:4403 as 'Publish · too-large' (280x812). Heading 'This page is too big to publish.' Meta: 'index.html is 2.4 MB; the limit is 2 MB per page. Optimised images are stored inside the page instead of being uploaded.' Actions: 'Open Media' (primary text link) and 'Try again'. Caption: 'The shipping build prints the raw Zod sentence "Page HTML exceeds 2097152 bytes" (packages/shared/schemas/publish.ts:30) — this board is what it should say.'

claim: Board 784:4250 draws no way to cancel a running publish; W-D-14 reads that as a design gap, on the grounds that 'cancellation is built end to end'.
truth: Correction to W-D-14, in the design's favour. Cancellation is built on the SERVER end to end, and the editor's own cancel function exists — but it has zero call sites: nothing in the editor ever calls it. So drawing a Cancel on this board is not a wiring fix, it is a feature request with a code cost. Separately, the CANCELLED terminal state has no branch in the panel at all: uiState 'cancelled' is neither publishing, nor failed, nor just-published, so the panel silently falls back to its idle body with no statement that the deploy was stopped.
evidence: Server: publish.service.ts cancelPublish (:412-431) + sites.cancelPublish (server/trpc/routers/sites.ts:405-427, ADMIN); worker checkCancelled at route.ts:246-251 and :356,:363,:370,:377,:385. Editor: PublishService.ts:124-126 cancelPublish; usePublishJob.ts:97 declares `cancel` and :227-237 implements it. Grep of packages/editor/src for `.cancel(` and `cancel:` outside usePublishJob returns only the declaration — no consumer. The missing branch: PublishUiState includes 'cancelled' (usePublishJob.ts:33, set at :304-305) and PublishTab reads only `uiState === 'publishing' | 'published' | 'failed'` (:148, :218, :224). W-D-19 already filed the missing cancelled board.
edit: No board change here. Amend the W-D-14 note so the coordinator prices it correctly: adding Cancel to 784:4250 requires a new call site for usePublishJob's `cancel`, which today has none. If the cancelled board from W-D-19 is drawn, note on it that PublishTab has no `cancelled` branch either — the panel would need one.

claim: Board 914:4507 'Publish · Confirm' draws four rows — Target, Pages, Client approval, Rollback — then a warning band and Back / Publish now.

Target reads the live URL or the blocking check; Pages is the EXPORTER's count, not the page list's; Client approval reads the real review round including the changes-requested branch; Rollback names the version and the 20-version retention. The board's 'Approved 2 Jul' is a sample — the product says 'Approved by <name> on 2 Jul' — which is shape-compatible.

Both entry points: PublishWizard.tsx:246-252 (panel path) and AquibraStudio.tsx:766-777 (topbar path, opened by requestPublish at :423-425 and wired at :521). The retention constant it cites is real: publish.service.ts:437 and the prune at :459-472.

claim: Board 1168:4713 'Publish · stale-approval' lists CHANGED SINCE APPROVAL as page + a semantic summary — 'Home / hero copy + image', 'Menu / 3 items re-priced', 'Contact / form field added' — and ends at the two buttons.
truth: The second column can only ever be one of three words. The modal diffs the approved page snapshot against the current export by comparing whole HTML strings, so a changed page yields exactly 'edited', 'added' or 'removed' — never what changed inside it. The board also omits a line the product does render and that answers the question the dialog raises: whether publishing anyway throws the sign-off away.

claim: Board 1168:4732 'Publish · issues-confirm' lists three page-scoped findings — 'Home · hero image missing alt text', 'Contact · form has no submit action', 'Menu · heading order skips a level' — plus '+1 more warning'.

The issues list has exactly ONE producer in the whole editor: the design-system TOKEN linter. Every issue it emits has its location hardcoded to `Brand › <tokenId>`, so a real row reads 'Brand › color.accent · Contrast below 4.5:1'. Not one of the three rows the board draws — an image without alt text, a form with no submit action, a skipped heading level — can be produced by anything in either tree. The board draws an accessibility/content linter that does not exist, inside the one dialog whose entire job is to name what is about to ship broken. (The separate omission I filed first — the missing open-review sentence — still stands and is folded in below.)

Bridge the one real source we have (designSystem.lintState) into it.' Grep of packages/editor/src for `setIssues` outside tests returns exactly this call site plus LintState.ts:67 (the linter's own per-token setter). The consumer chain is state.issues (useStudioState.ts:254,:490) → AquibraStudio.tsx:500 → StudioHeader.tsx:184,:572-573 (errorCount/warnCount) → :683 confirmRows → the rows at :879-902, which print `{i.location ? i.location + ' · ' : ''}{i.message}`. The omitted sentence is StudioHeader.tsx:872-878.

claim: Board 1172:4825 is titled 'Export site as HTML' with the HTML pill selected and the CTA 'Export as HTML', and its subtitle reads 'A .zip with every page, styles inlined, media included — host it anywhere.'
truth: The subtitle describes a different format from the one the board has selected, and it is not accurate about that format either. The HTML format produces ONE file — the active page, styles inlined, no media bundled. The ZIP format produces every page plus a SEPARATE styles.css and an assets/ folder — so 'styles inlined' is wrong for the ZIP too. The shipping modal already fixed this by making the sentence per-format.

claim: MOD-A-12 states that exportPublishPages calls exportAllPages without includeSitemap or baseUrl, and concludes 'a publish emits no sitemap at all', instructing that any board promising a sitemap be marked unimplemented.
truth: Half right, and the conclusion is wrong. The ENGINE's sitemap option is indeed never set by any caller — so a downloaded ZIP and a single-file export ship no sitemap. But a PUBLISH does emit one: the dashboard worker builds the deploy file set itself and adds sitemap.xml plus robots.txt with a Sitemap: directive, gated on the site's allowIndexing and a resolvable origin. No board in section 1776:8378 promises a sitemap, so nothing here needs marking — but the instruction must not be applied on MOD-A-12's strength.
evidence: Engine side: ExportEngine.ts:54-57 declares includeSitemap/baseUrl, :726-731 is the only consumer, and the only two callers pass neither — exportPublishPages.ts:39 `exportAllPages({ format: 'html', minify: true })` and ExportEngine.ts:1101 `exportAllPages({ format: 'html', minify: cfg.minify })`. Server side: lib/publish-files.ts:82-84 `if (input.allowIndexing && input.origin) files.push({ file: 'sitemap.xml', data: buildSitemapXml(...) })` and :75-78 robots.txt with `withSitemapDirective`; buildSitemapXml at lib/publish-urls.ts:85-107 (it also drops noindex pages, :92). Called from the worker at route.ts:346-360.
edit: No board change. Correct the MOD-A-12 note in the shared record: a publish DOES ship sitemap.xml (lib/publish-files.ts:82) unless indexing is off or no origin resolves; the ZIP and single-file exports do not.

claim: Nothing in section 1776:8378 draws a rate-limited publish, and no board hints at one.
truth: Correct, and correct to leave it that way. There is no rate limit on publishing. The only throttle is structural: a partial unique index allows one active job per site, and a second attempt is refused with ALREADY_PUBLISHING (see FIG-C-11). Nothing counts publishes per user, per workspace or per window.
evidence: server/trpc/routers/sites.ts:313-385 — the publish mutation has a role check and the startPublish call, and no rate-limit middleware; grepped the router and publish.service.ts for a limiter and found none. The only refusal path is publish.service.ts:196-208 (the in-flight query) plus the P2002 translation at :348-351, and the stale-row cleanup at :215-234 that keeps a dead job from blocking future publishes forever.
edit: No change. Recorded so no future pass invents a rate-limit board.

claim: No board distinguishes a simulated publish from a real one.
truth: Nor should one. The simulation path exists but is behind an explicit opt-in that must never be true in production, and it is already made visible in the one place a user would look: it returns a URL on the RFC-2606 reserved .invalid TLD, so the panel's Production row reads e.g. 'bella-cucina.dev-simulated.invalid'. The five build steps still animate and the outcome toast still says 'Published — site is live'. That is a deliberate dev-only affordance, not a product state that needs designing.

The panel renders it through domainOf (usePublishSnapshot.ts:78-85, :175).

claim: Board 817:4856 (1080x540) draws 'Preview interaction testing — 5 feedback types' plus a 'Preview console' logging nav / hover / form / warn events. The five types are Link navigation ('Clicking a link navigates within preview. Back/forward browser buttons work'), Hover states, Form submission ('Submit triggers validation UI ... Success shows green toast'), Scroll & anchor ('Smooth scroll to anchor links ... Parallax effects play'), and Broken element ('External scripts blocked (security)').
truth: Read properly with a stack walk (30 text nodes, not the 4-ish a name-only reading suggests), the board makes five separable claims and the preview refutes four of them by construction. Link navigation: impossible — the preview renders the ACTIVE PAGE ONLY into a srcDoc iframe; there is no second page, no router and no history. Form submission: impossible in the strongest sense — every <form> is REMOVED from the document, so there is nothing to submit or validate. Parallax: impossible — it is script-driven and every <script> is stripped, and the iframe is sandbox="" besides. Preview console: nothing logs anything anywhere. Hover states is the one that genuinely works, being pure CSS. And 'External scripts blocked (security)' is accidentally true but understates it: ALL scripts are blocked, internal ones included, which is exactly why the other four fail.
evidence: Sanitizer: ExportUtils.ts:36-42 `doc.querySelectorAll('script,iframe,object,embed,link,meta[http-equiv],base,form').forEach(n => { if (n.tagName === 'LINK' && isAllowedStylesheet(n)) return; n.remove(); })`. Active page only: AquibraStudio.tsx:205 `composer.exportHTML().combined` → Composer.ts:656 → ElementManager.ts:273-275 → HTMLParser.ts:39-49 (`ctx.getActivePageId()`, one root). Sandbox: PreviewOverlay.tsx:106 `sandbox=""`. The runtime that is stripped: Composer.ts:696-704, spliced at :715; it works on the published page (ExportEngine.ts:864-866). Producer/consumer checked by constant, not call site: UI_TOGGLE_PREVIEW is emitted at StudioHeader.tsx:359 and handled only at AquibraStudio.tsx:199-207. Grepped for a preview console/event log — no producer.
edit: Rename 817:4856 to '[not-implemented] Preview · interaction test — the preview strips every <script> and every <form> (ExportUtils.ts:36-42) and renders the active page alone in a sandbox="" iframe, so link navigation, form submission, parallax and the event console are all impossible there; only Hover states works, and interactions do work on the published page'. On the board, mark the Hover states card as the one shipped behaviour and leave the other four as the spec they are.

claim: Board 817:4899 (280x812) draws an Accessibility panel with a score of 72, a 3 Errors / 5 Warnings / 12 Passed summary, eight findings each with its own fix button ('Fix contrast', 'Add alt text', 'Fix heading', 'Increase size', 'Add label', 'Add focus style', 'Add text label', 'Add media query'), and two passing checks.
truth: Read properly (36 text nodes), this is a complete feature spec, and none of it has a producer. There is no a11y rule engine in either tree — no axe, no contrast computation, no alt-text audit, no heading-order check, no tap-target measurement, no focus-ring detection. The only accessibility artefact in the product is a stylesheet of focus-visible and reduced-motion rules. Note also that this board is not a standalone feature: its score of 72 is the same 72 that appears as the 'Accessibility' tile on the site-audit board 817:4950, so 817:4899 is that audit's Accessibility drill-down and shares its (nonexistent) producer.
evidence: Grepped both trees case-insensitively for accessibilityCheck | a11yCheck | axe-core | contrastCheck | altTextAudit — zero hits outside tests; for 'missing alt' | 'alt text' | 'heading order' | headingOrder across packages/editor/src every hit is media alt-text AUTHORING (AssetDetailOverlay.tsx:275,:379, MediaContextMenu.tsx:225, AltTextService.ts:27), never a rule. The only a11y home is src/themes/design-system/a11y.css, named as the canonical a11y-rules file in packages/editor/CLAUDE.md's DS SSOT table. The one issue producer that does exist is the DS token linter and it emits Brand › <tokenId> rows only (AquibraStudio.tsx:307-328) — see FIG-C-16. Shared score read off both boards with the stack walk: 817:4899 '72' and 817:4950 '72 / Accessibility'.
edit: Rename 817:4899 to '[not-implemented] Preview · accessibility checker — no a11y rule engine exists in either tree (no axe, no contrast, alt-text, heading-order, tap-target or focus checks); the only a11y artefact is themes/design-system/a11y.css. This is the Accessibility drill-down of the site-audit board 817:4950 and shares its missing producer.' Add a cross-link annotation between 817:4899 and 817:4950 so they are read as one feature.

claim: Four boards draw a complete site audit: 817:4950 (four category tiles — Performance 91, Accessibility 72, Best Practices 95, SEO 88 — six Lighthouse metrics from First Contentful Paint to Time to Interactive, and four recommendations with per-fix savings), 879:6896 ('Running site audit… Lighthouse checks performance, accessibility, best practices, and SEO on the published version. Takes about 30 seconds.'), 879:6901 (an issue drill-down with per-file byte estimates and a 'Convert all to WebP' action), and 1157:4593 (the all-clear).
truth: Read properly (36 / 2 / 7 / 26 text nodes), this is a precise design for a slot that exists in the product, is named, and is deliberately never filled. The publish worker's pipeline has a step literally called 'Performance check (Lighthouse)'; it is in SKIPPED_STEPS, so it reports 'skipped' and never 'done', and lighthouseScore stays null. The publish result schema carries a lighthouseScore field that nothing anywhere writes. 879:6896's own sentence — 'on the published version' — names exactly where that slot sits. So the right label is not a vague design-ahead: it is 'the pipeline step exists and is switched off'. Nothing measures FCP, LCP, TBT, CLS, Speed Index or TTI, and nothing sizes an image for a savings estimate.
evidence: worker route.ts:21-27 STEPS = ['Generating pages','Optimizing images','Deploying to CDN','Verifying SSL','Performance check']; :29-37 `SKIPPED_STEPS = new Set([1, 4])` with 'Steps that are NOT actually run in the MVP. They must report "skipped", never "done" — a green checkmark for work that didn't happen is a false signal (image optimization and the Lighthouse performance check both come later)'; :42-51 buildSteps maps a skipped index to 'skipped'; :389-392 'Step 4 — Performance check (Lighthouse): not run in MVP ... lighthouseScore stays null'. The field with no writer: packages/shared/schemas/publish.ts:68 `lighthouseScore: z.number().nullable()`. Grepped both trees for performanceAudit | perfAudit | pageSpeed — zero hits; for 'lighthouse' — five hits, four in that worker file plus one test assertion (route.buildSteps.test.ts:20 asserts the step is 'skipped').
edit: Append to all four board names: '— no performance measurement exists. The publish worker HAS a "Performance check (Lighthouse)" step and it is in SKIPPED_STEPS (route.ts:29-37), so it always reports skipped; publishResultSchema.lighthouseScore (publish.ts:68) has no writer.' Keep all four boards — this is the spec for a named, empty slot. Also cross-link 817:4950's Accessibility tile to 817:4899 (same score, same missing producer).

claim: Board 817:4774 is already labelled '[not-implemented · superseded by 988:2 · Site · Access] Preview · share link'. Two of the six controls are fully backed by the service that owns share links — expiry and password both exist, and both are plan-gated with their own refusals. The other two are backed by nothing: no QR code is generated anywhere in the editor or the dashboard for a share link, and there is no email-invite path on a share link at all. So the board is not uniformly not-implemented; half of it is real and living on another board, and half of it is unbacked anywhere.
evidence: Real: server/services/share-link.service.ts:12-15 `createShareLink(siteId, data: { name, password?, expiresInDays? }, userId?)`; expiry written at :62-66 (`expiresAt.setDate(... + data.expiresInDays)`) and plan-capped at :38-40 (`EXPIRY_EXCEEDS_PLAN` against `limits.shareLinkExpiryMaxDays`); password hashed at :56-60 and plan-gated at :43-45 (`PASSWORD_LINKS_NOT_AVAILABLE` against `limits.shareLinkPasswords`); also a FREE-plan cap of 3 links per site at :47-51. Unbacked: grepped both trees case-insensitively for qrcode | qr_code | \bqr\b — the only hits are an icon-catalogue entry (icons.ts:272,:739,:883) and the dashboard's 2FA setup, which builds its QR from api.qrserver.com for an otpauth URI (security-tab.tsx:227); nothing does this for a share link. No email-invite function exists on the share-link service — its whole exported surface is listShareLinks (:5), createShareLink (:12) and revokeShareLink (:79).
edit: Extend the board name's clause to record the split: '... — same hand-off; share links are owned by access-tab.tsx + share-link.service.ts. Expiry and password are REAL there (createShareLink, both plan-gated); the QR code and Invite-via-email drawn here are backed by nothing in either tree.' claim: Section 1779:4 '14 · Preview' contains seven boards and not one of them draws the preview the product actually ships. All seven draw preview features that do not exist.
truth: The shipping preview lives on two boards in other sections — 65:211 'Shell state 7 · Preview' (section 1776:8385) and 807:8663 'S3.8 · preview-responsive · mobile-device-frame' (section 23) — and neither records what the preview DOES to the document. Four facts about it are load-bearing and drawn nowhere: it renders the ACTIVE PAGE ONLY, with no navigation to other pages; it strips script, iframe, object, embed, form, base and meta[http-equiv], keeping only <style> and a fonts.googleapis.com stylesheet; it runs no CMS resolution, so a bound element previews with its placeholder while the published page shows the entry; and the iframe is fully sandboxed. Anyone reading this section today would conclude the preview is unbuilt.
evidence: Active page only: AquibraStudio.tsx:205 `composer.exportHTML().combined` → Composer.ts:656 `this.elements.toHTML(options)` → ElementManager.ts:273-275 → HTMLParser.ts:39-49, which resolves `ctx.getActivePageId()` and returns that one root (and ignores its options argument, `_options`). Stripping: ExportUtils.ts:36-42 and the head rebuild at :94-95 `return '<!DOCTYPE html><html><head><meta charset="utf-8">' + fontLinks + styles + '</head>' + body`. No CMS resolve: Composer.exportHTML (:655-720) never touches cmsResolver, while both export paths do — ExportEngine.ts:185-188 (single file) and :709-712 (publish). Sandbox: PreviewOverlay.tsx:106 `sandbox=""`. Device switch: PreviewOverlay.tsx:71,:99-101,:103.
edit: Create one board in section 1779:4, 1080x540, named 'Preview · what the sandbox drops (reference)', placed first in the section. It draws two columns: LEFT, a small annotated copy of the shipping overlay (topbar retained, 40-tall device bar with the breakpoint switcher, the page on the app ground, the dark 'Done' pill bottom-centre) pointing at 65:211 and 807:8663 as the canonical boards; RIGHT, a plain list of what the preview is NOT — 'active page only, no navigation', 'no scripts: interactions never run', 'no forms', 'no iframes or embeds', 'no CMS resolution: bindings show placeholders', 'fonts.googleapis.com is the only external stylesheet kept'. Each line carries its file:line. This board is a reference, not a UI to build.
